stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a major LLM model.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current models being restricted to a single robot embodiment.
Enables training on diverse, internet-scale videos (human and robotic) to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, indicating a modern LLM architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core NLP task of text generation within the AI/ML ecosystem.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically engineered for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is designed to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured $88M in funding from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
The company serves a substantial developer base, currently reaching 8.9 million developers.
The funding validates the growing importance and adoption of open-source large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon through updates to its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs and faster response times.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating active development.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries (AI Overviews) on search results pages.
This expansion pushes traditional organic search links significantly further down the results page.
The change represents a continued integration and prioritization of generative AI within core search functionality.

stories.title: Anthropic was illegally blacklisted by the Trump administration, court rules
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: A court ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of AI lab Anthropic by the Trump administration was unconstitutional.
The lawsuit alleged unlawful retaliation against Anthropic by the Trump administration.
The ruling represents a significant legal victory for Anthropic in a high-profile legal battle.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that Trump's blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed involvement in lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance.
The ruling highlights legal challenges surrounding government attempts to restrict AI development based on ideological grounds.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two alleged members of the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP conducted a large-scale, relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in product execution harnesses, where harmful tool use is a greater threat than simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current automatic red-teaming methods, specifically the risk of retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack coordination.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by simulating real-world corporate communication complexity without requiring proprietary data sharing.
Evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a massive corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, focusing on temporal knowledge.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA) to adapt advertising for Generative AI.
LAMA embeds advertiser influence directly into the token generation process, moving beyond traditional slots.
Advertisers report local continuation values to induce advertiser-specific next-token policies.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with the open-source ecosystem via Ollama.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma redefined 'Project Helix' from a singular console to a 'family of devices'.
This signals a potential shift in Microsoft's hardware strategy for its next-generation gaming platform.
The announcement suggests a broader ecosystem approach rather than a single monolithic console release.

stories.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The EPA is planning to remove a federal rule requiring public notice for certain industrial sites.
This change specifically impacts data centers, allowing them potentially to hide air pollution.
The move comes amid growing community backlash regarding the environmental impact of new data centers.

stories.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia’s AI effects on everything
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An unofficial version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 has been leaked and is being tested by modders.
The leaked code was reportedly found in an early-access build of NBA 2K27.
Modders are applying the AI upscaling technology to popular games like Skyrim and Cyberpunk 2077.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature in its AI glasses to prevent unauthorized recording.
The glasses will cease recording if the user covers the designated safety light.
This update addresses privacy concerns related to the device's recording capabilities.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience into persistent, reusable skills.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through continuous interaction and knowledge consolidation.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper introduces SWE-Prime to address limitations in current LLM training for software engineering tasks.
It critiques the existing method of using large-scale agent trajectory datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), noting that 'success' does not imply 'quality'.
SWE-Prime aims to mitigate noisy supervision by addressing ineffective, redundant, or risky steps present in successful trajectories.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review systems often treat the process as a single, static decision, which is an oversimplification.
Real-world code review is inherently an iterative and multi-round interactive process between developers and reviewers.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the complex, dynamic nature of actual software code review.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions.
MAELLE models reactions not as molecular edits, but as discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors.
This approach addresses the limitation of existing ML methods that rely on molecule generation or topological graph edits.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architecture pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining auditable, traceable execution.
Proposes separating persona (in a single-homed trust domain) from execution (in a faceless, audited domain) via a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluation, which often only measure successful judgments.
The study benchmarks three specific scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) using a controlled, artifact-backed synthetic corpus.
The evaluation covers 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts across 145 specimen families, testing for binary security ground truth.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
A two-site retrospective study was conducted on nearly 37,000 adult patients to develop a new, learned sepsis severity score.
The study aims to create a continuous severity score directly derived from patient trajectories, moving beyond coarse, historical calibrations.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study uses six independent linear probes, corresponding to the six categories of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT), to test model capabilities.
The core question is whether LLMs can geometrically distinguish between different moral foundations and the relationships between them.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses a critical clinical gap by developing a continuous sepsis severity score, moving beyond outdated, fixed-variable indices.
The study is a retrospective, two-site validation across two distinct hospital systems, lending practical relevance.
The methodology involves learning directly from patient trajectories, representing an advancement in time-series clinical prediction models.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study uses six independent linear probes, mapping to the six categories of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT).
The goal is to determine if LLMs organize these moral foundations geometrically and distinguish between them.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for academia and open-source communities.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a method demonstrating cost-efficient LLM training using consumer-grade hardware (RTX 5090).
Contrasts the new approach with the prohibitive costs of training existing models like Llama-3.2-3B and SmolLM3-3B.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It systematically analyzes the optimization dynamics of ES to compare its performance against established methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates that ES offers a performance advantage over GRPO in certain reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to boost LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different model scales within the same family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences into persistent, reusable skills.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through continuous interaction and knowledge persistence.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of noisy supervision when training LLMs to fix real-world software bugs using successful agent trajectories.
Prior methods rely on large-scale trajectory datasets and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), but successful paths can still contain inefficient or risky steps.
SWE-Prime proposes a method to improve LLM performance by mitigating the negative impact of suboptimal steps present in existing successful trajectories.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in current LLM post-training methods like RL and OPSD.
Existing methods require ground-truth labels, which prevents effective test-time training (TTT) for improving mathematical reasoning.
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels as a replacement for ground truth, while analyzing the inherent fragility and asymmetric failure modes of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review against its real-world, iterative, and multi-round interactive nature.
The research aims to improve the accuracy and realism of automated code review by modeling the complex problem-solving inherent in human developer interactions.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a known issue in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain generative diversity during the RLVR process.
This work offers a simple yet effective method to improve LLM exploration and performance (pass@$k$) without relying solely on existing algorithmic regularizations.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study uses linear probes trained on open-weight models to test for the geometric organization of different Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
This work delves into the internal reasoning mechanisms of LLMs regarding complex ethical concepts.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world problem: clinical language models fail in deployment due to overfitting to note-specific artifacts (templates, boilerplate).
Introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework designed for auditable clinical text classification.
Utilizes Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract sparse, human-auditable features from Transformer activations, improving robustness.

stories.title: Stop Wrestling with ASR: The Complete Guide to Gemini 3.5 Transcribe 🎙️
stories.author: giom_v
bullet_points: The article focuses on Gemini 3.5's transcription capabilities (ASR).
It targets developers looking to integrate advanced audio processing into their applications.
The guide aims to simplify the use of Gemini for tasks like summarizing podcasts and video analysis.
